subject: URGENT: Lumen - AZ1 latency & 5xx surge / request for geo-drain
messages:
From: Alexa Jones <alexa.jones@lumen.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike in AZ1

Mina —

We're seeing sustained 5xx rates on our traffic routed to AZ1 starting ~07:45 UTC. Tail latency for token generation has jumped from ~120ms to 1.6s and error rate is ~3.8% over the last 20min (see attached chart). This is impacting transaction throughput for our checkout flows.

Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-local degradation or something on your side? We need a remediation path ASAP — at minimum a regional redirect to eastus2 for traffic originating in our US region.

Alexa
SRE, Lumen Communications

Attachments: lumen_az1_error_rate_chart.png, az1-500-logs-snippet.txt

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Jones <alexa.jones@lumen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike in AZ1

Alexa —

Thanks for the signal and the logs. We're seeing the same metrics on our side: AZ1 (us-east-1a) is experiencing increased queue waits on the runtime layer leading to timeouts that cascade into 5xx responses. Initial triage shows a runaway batching job on a subset of pods and elevated context switches on a single shard.

Immediate proposal (can action in ~6–8 minutes with your go-ahead):
- Geo-drain: shift new Lumen requests away from AZ1 -> eastus2 for the US region (gradual 30% -> 100% in 5min steps).
- Hold cached KV invalidations until after warmup to avoid cold-start amplification.
- Route fallback: keep AZ1 in passive standby for small percentage of non-latency-critical traffic.

I'll coordinate the rollout with Rishi + Hannah and loop back with exact ETA. If you approve the geo-drain, please confirm now. We'll also prepare a short MAP for post-incident remediation/follow-up.

—Mina
Platform Reliability (Redwood Inference)

Quoted excerpt: "On Tue, 29 Jun 2027, Alexa Jones wrote:"
"> Mina —
"> We're seeing sustained 5xx rates on our traffic routed to AZ1 starting ~07:45 UTC...

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike in AZ1

Actionable notes from infra: we ran quick diagnostics —
- One inference shard in AZ1 is saturated due to a combination of a long-running high-seq decode and poor kernel queuing (suspected kernel memory pressure).
- KV cache hit rates are normal; this is not a cold-cache event.
- Estimated user impact: 3–6% request failure for Lumen's traffic if left unmitigated; higher tail latency for multimodal calls.

Plan (ops steps):
1) Initiate traffic steering policy: 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 6 minutes across our load balancer.
2) Evict the problematic shard (cordon + restart with kernel tuning) and replace with a warmed instance; this will take ~12m but runs asynchronously.
3) Apply per-tenant throttles for heavy gen sessions to protect global pool.

Risks & mitigations:
- Short-term increased latency while eastus2 warms for large sequences — mitigate by ramping slowly and keeping 10% traffic sampled to verify correctness.
- Client-side retries may amplify load; recommend telling Lumen to hold non-essential retries during the drain window.

I can run the steer now pending exec approval for priority capacity bump (we'll pull dedicated burst capacity for ~20min).

—Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike in AZ1 — exec ask

Vivek —

Lumen (strategic account, ~USD 120k/mo) is experiencing a regional AZ failure that's currently causing checkout failures for a subset of customers. Rishi's gone through root cause and we recommend an immediate geo-drain and a short dedicated burst capacity allocation (20min) to eastus2 while we recycle the problematic shard.

Ask: approve priority capacity and waive any rate-metering for the next 30 minutes so we can route Lumen traffic with minimal throttling. We'll capture cost impact and propose a goodwill SLA credit if the postmortem shows platform-side regression. Attached is a short mutual action plan (MAP) I drafted that we can share with the customer after confirmation.

If approved, ops will start the 30%->100% steer immediately and provide live metrics via the Confluence incident page.

—Marissa
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_lumen.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Jones <alexa.jones@lumen.com>, Lumen SRE Team <sre-team@lumen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-29T12:46:00Z
Subject: ACTIONED: Geo-drain to eastus2 initiated / next steps & postmortem

Alexa —

Thanks again for the alert and for the logs. With Vivek's approval (internal), we initiated the geo-drain at 12:30 UTC and ramped to 100% traffic to eastus2 at 12:36 UTC. Early telemetry shows error rate for Lumen dropping back to <0.5% and tail latency reducing toward baseline.

What we did:
- 12:30 UTC: 30% traffic steer away from AZ1.
- 12:33 UTC: 60% ramp.
- 12:36 UTC: 100% redirect to eastus2; problematic shard cordoned and restart triggered.

Next steps:
- We will run the shard replacement and kernel-tune cycle tonight; full postmortem & timeline posted to the Confluence incident page within 24 hours.
- Proposing a 1% goodwill credit while we finish the investigation; Marissa will follow up on commercials.
- Please keep non-essential retries paused for the next 30 minutes to avoid amplification.

I'll keep this thread updated and schedule a 30-min post-incident call tomorrow 14:00 UTC to walk through remediation.

—Mina Haddad
Platform Reliability (Redwood Inference)
